In contrast, the pond with the DIC solution feeding system consumed on average 15.8 g/d CO , ranging from 8.4 to 24.5 g/d, indicating a 90% 2 improvement in the CO utilization efficiency (CUE) on average (Figure G3-7). 2 Similar results were obtained in a second, 20-day cultivation of WT N. oceanica with the CO transfer system in recirculation mode. When the pH in the storage tank was 2 above 6, the pH controller turned on the pump to circulate the solution through the membrane contactor until the pH reached 6. The DIC solution in the storage tank was pumped into the cultivation pond to control pH at 8.0. During the 20-day cultivation, the algal cell growth as measured by turbidity (OD750) in the mini-raceway ponds, one using CO sparging and the other using the DIC 2 solution feeding system, were statistically the same (Figure G3-8). As before, the DIC concentration in the DIC solution feeding system mini-pond was higher than in the CO sparging system mini-pond in the first 8 days of cultivation (Figure G3-9). 2 However, the DIC concentrations were at similar levels in both ponds in the next 12 days of cultivation. As shown in Figure G3-10, the CO consumption in the CO sparging system was 2 2 significantly higher than that of the DIC solution feeding system during the 20 days of cultivation. In the CO sparging system, the daily CO consumption was in the 2 2 range of 17.9 to 72.8 g/d, averaging 40.9 g/d per 75-L cultivation. In contrast, the pond with the DIC solution feeding system consumed on average about 16.7 g/d CO , ranging from 10.7 to 25.2 g/d. The CUE in the DIC solution feeding system 2 pond was 53.6% while the CUE in the CO sparging pond was 28.9% (Figure G3- 2 11). Therefore, the CUE was improved by 85% by using the DIC solution system. The algal biomass from both mini-ponds was collected at the end of the cultivation and freeze-dried to analyze the algal biomass composition. The DIC solution feeding resulted in higher protein content and lower carbohydrate content than those of the CO sparging system (Figure G3-12). There was no significant difference in ash 2 content and lipid content. The FAME profile analysis showed that the DIC solution feeding resulted in higher C16:0 and C16:1 content than those of the CO sparging 2 system, while the C20:5n3 was significantly lower. Similar results were also obtained when the direct feeding configuration (Figure G3- 1) was used in a 2-week cultivation in mini-raceway ponds. The algal growth was similar whether using CO sparging or the DIC solution feeding system (Figure G3- 2 13). The OD750 and cell dry weight reached the highest at Day 12 in both cases.
